summary.headline: Nykaa Q4 FY26 net revenue rose 28% YoY to INR 2,648 crore with EBITDA margin of 8.4% and PAT of INR 79 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 GMV and net revenue both grew 28% YoY, with net revenue of INR 2,648 crore and gross margin of 45.4%. EBITDA reached INR 223 crore (8.4% of net revenue, up 67% YoY) and PAT INR 79 crore. FY26 net revenue crossed INR 10,000 crore, with EBITDA at 7.5% and PAT at 2.0% of net revenue. Fashion turned EBITDA positive at 0.3% in Q4, and Beauty EBITDA margin was 10.3% in Q4. Management said April and May were good, but flagged oil prices, currency and inflation as reasons for caution for the next year.

segments.name: Beauty (vertical)
segments.commentary: FY26 GMV close to INR 15,000 crore (+27%), NSV about INR 8,500 crore, EBITDA margin 9.6% (+70 bps). Q4 GMV +27%, NSV +29%, EBITDA margin 10.3%.

segments.name: House of Nykaa (owned brands)
segments.commentary: FY26 GMV INR 3,176 crore (~+50%); Beauty part INR 2,788 crore (+65%). Dot & Key INR 1,790 crore GMV, Kay Beauty ~INR 380 crore (3x in 3 years), Nykaa Cosmetics ~INR 400 crore.

segments.name: Superstore (B2B)
segments.commentary: Business of ~INR 1,200 crore GMV built in 4 years, ~0.5 million retailers across 1,300 cities, 220+ brands. Almost 30% of orders self-placed by retailers. Management said EBITDA margin improved by more than 500 bps.

segments.name: Nykaa Fashion
segments.commentary: FY26 GMV almost INR 5,000 crore (+30%), NSV INR 1,447 crore (~+30%). EBITDA margin improved from -8.3% to -2.6% for FY26; Q4 EBITDA was +0.3% with Q4 NSV growth of 42%.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance given; management said April and May growth momentum was good.

Beauty: each sub-business (multi-brand retail, House of Brands, B2B Superstore) to keep improving margin; management expects similar year-over-year margin trajectory in coming years while reinvesting in growth.
B2B Superstore expected to be a single-digit margin business at steady state; owned brands could have higher margins than multi-brand retail.
Beauty retail store additions planned at about 50-60 per year, with about 170-180 more doors over 2-3 years toward a 500-store target in 3-4 years.
Fashion: management expects margin trajectory to remain positive; did not give long-term numbers.
Nykaa Now (quick commerce) to be marketed more actively in FY27 after building about 75-80 dark stores across top 7 metros.
Company annual day in about six weeks to detail the house-of-brands plan.
capex_capacity: Capex utilisation at about 1% of revenue, with investment in beauty retail store expansion, fulfilment and technology.
Beauty store network about 313 stores across 99 cities, over 3 lakh sq ft; more than doubled over 3 years. Like-for-like growth double digit in FY26.
Earth Rhythm: acquired additional 24% stake to complete 100% ownership (had 76% from FY23-FY25) at pre-agreed terms.
Took over Kiehl's India boutique and online operations in the quarter; also building Charlotte Tilbury exclusive brand stores.
Fixed asset turnover improved to 9.9x in FY26 from 9.1x in FY25.
demand_pricing: Beauty: 1.8 billion visits to website/app in FY26 (+28%); 45 million monthly active unique visitors; 19.7 million annual transacting customers; 66 million orders vs 36 million in FY23.
Korean beauty brands grew 58% YoY on platform; dermacosmetics GMV grew over 40% YoY.

Fashion: new customer acquisition up 41% YoY; over 1,200-1,300 brands added in the last year; men's category +60%, kids +50%, home +40%. H&M is now the number one brand on Nykaa Fashion since its November launch; Nike onboarded and Nykaa manages Nike.com and app in India from February.
Management said AOV growth has been muted in recent quarters because new customers (lower AOV) form a larger share of transacting customers; focus is on frequency and annual consumption value.
Brands may pull back on digital ad spend if inflation persists; management said no single brand accounts for double-digit revenue.
Imports are a small share of direct sourcing; forex is fully hedged for the next 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for next year across segments, and the impact of inflation on demand and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Falguni Nayar said April and May were good, but high oil prices, a weaker currency and inflation make management cautious. She added that beauty is a small luxury and AI is helping both top line and costs.

qa_highlights.question: How are new visitors rising while marketing spend is controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Anchit Nayar cited a focus on new customer acquisition for 4-6 quarters, app experience improvements, and AI-driven efficiency in paid acquisition on Meta and Google and in personalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state margins for Beauty sub-businesses and Fashion, and freight/fuel cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said each beauty business is improving margin, but reinvestment in growth continues, and B2B is a single-digit margin business. Brands have not yet passed on price increases, though a price rise is possible.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Fashion growth to 30% while marketing fell, and has competition eased?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhijeet Dabas credited higher repeat frequency, new-customer acquisition and marquee brands such as H&M and Nike. He said competition has not abated, but Nykaa Fashion focuses on premium online fashion, with a $55 billion TAM.

qa_highlights.question: Can private label rise to 30% of BPC without hurting third-party brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Anchit Nayar disputed the 20% figure and said owned brands do not account for 20% of retail revenue. Adwaita Nayar said the aim is building an independent house of brands, not raising Nykaa's share.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook for Dot & Key and other owned brands after a high base, and AUTC vs AOV growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Adwaita Nayar said growth will come from existing brands plus breakout brands (4 meaningful brands now). Anchit Nayar said customer acquisition headroom remains large and AOV growth is expected to come from personalisation and premiumisation.

qa_highlights.question: Rupee exposure of imported brands, and Nykaa Now salience?
qa_highlights.answer: P. Ganesh said direct imports are a small share and forex is hedged for 2-3 months. Anchit Nayar said about 75-80 rapid stores cover the top 7 metros, with a 30-minute to 2-hour promise, and that marketing starts in FY27.

risks_watch: Macro: high oil prices, currency depreciation and inflation could hit consumption and brand ad budgets.
Brands may pass on price increases or reduce digital ad spend, affecting AOV and marketing revenue.
Owned-brand growth at 65% from a concentrated base (Dot & Key ~INR 1,790 crore GMV) may slow; management avoided a numeric growth target.
Margin trajectory depends on mix: B2B Superstore is lower-margin and could dilute the Beauty vertical.
Fashion EBITDA only just turned positive (+0.3% in Q4); sustainability is unproven.
Inference cost and AI spend were raised as a margin pressure but not quantified.
Store additions of ~50-60 a year and the Nykaa Now marketing ramp in FY27 need monitoring.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 results and momentum, with a cautious tone on the macro outlook (oil, currency, inflation). Management avoided quantitative FY27 guidance and deferred long-term numbers to the upcoming annual day.
key_quotes: we are really seeing continued growth momentum in both GMV, which grew at 28% year -on-year and net revenue, which grew also at a similar pace of 28% year-on-year.
Except for the general environmental concerns, we are not seeing any specific concerns yet, but it is hard to assume that they won't emerge as you go forward
Nowhere are we claiming that we will deliver 65% year -on-year growth forever for the next 5 years.
Our multi -brand retail relationships and commitments come first.

adds.what: Beauty retail stores: about 50-60 doors a year, ~170-180 more over 2-3 years toward 500-store target
Nykaa Now quick-commerce dark stores (~75-80 built across top 7 metros); marketing push in FY27

growth.why: No formal numerical revenue guidance; management said April and May growth momentum was good and plans about 50-60 Beauty doors a year (170-180 more over 2-3 years) with margin improvement in each business, backed by store capex and existing demand metrics, but flagged oil, currency and inflation risks.
